note: Three researched reference anchors, not a complete causal model. No troops, resources, authority, deaths, calendar advancement or scheduled effects are initialized. No simulation end date is imposed.
calendar_note: Dates retain the historical Julian convention used by this campaign. Day precision supplies no opening hour or within-day ordering.

sources.title: Henry V's letter announcing Harfleur's capture, 22 September 1415; Riley's edition of London Letter-Book I, reproduced by the University of Southampton
sources.locator: Memorials of London 1415, one-page reproduction; original Letter-Book I fol. cxliii; H. T. Riley (1868), pp. 601-624
sources.scope_note: Royal report of the 18 September negotiations and subsequent handover, dated 22 September. It is a partisan contemporary account, not an inventory or complete reconstruction. Its different siege-start date is not adopted here.

sources.title: The Hundred Years' War, Royal Armouries: Battle of Agincourt
sources.locator: The Battle of Agincourt, dated 25 October 1415
sources.scope_note: Supports the battle date, Henry's English army meeting French opposition and the English victory. No quantities, casualty totals or detailed tactical model are imported.

sources.title: Authored read-only conditional-plan assessment policy, revision 1
sources.scope_note: Condition bindings and dependency edges are explicit design inferences for review, not claims that sources establish an exhaustive causal model. Missing records remain unknown.

events.title: Harfleur surrender negotiations
events.description: Henry's subsequent letter reports negotiations and the delivery of hostages on 18 September.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: A conditional surrender arrangement was made while an opportunity for French relief remained.

events.title: Harfleur handover
events.description: Henry's letter dated 22 September reports the delivery of Harfleur's keys after no relieving battle occurred.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: The town passed into Henry's possession in the reported historical sequence.

events.title: Battle of Agincourt
events.description: Henry's returning army encountered French forces near Agincourt on 25 October 1415.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: The historical battle ended in an English victory; this is a reference outcome, not a campaign award.
